results.fact: Days of walking to reach Whatcom Pass
results.evidence: The 'three or four days' claim lives only in bivy[0] (Whatcom Camp, the trail-camp chain via Brush Creek, currently closed), which is a regional camp card; this route's itinerary reaches Perfect Pass on day 2 via Easy Ridge. Whatcom Camp does not serve this itinerary (closed, and the route goes Easy Ridge in); Perfect Pass does. No bivy patch per the camping clean-up ownership.

results.fact: Whether the overnight permit can be reserved
results.correct_value: Park permits are 60% reservable in general, but the Easy Ridge and Perfect Pass cross-country zones used by this itinerary are walk-up only (Perfect Pass: one party per night); US Cabin Camp is reservable.
results.evidence: The park's cross-country zone page lists Perfect Pass (party limit 6, one party per night) and Easy Ridge (4 parties per night) and states only Boston Basin, Eldorado, Sulphide, Price, Triumph and Tapto Lakes are reservable; the reservations page repeats that all other zones are walk-up only. The Recreation.gov permit system files Perfect Pass and Easy Ridge under ordinary 'Cross Country Zones (North)' rather than the reservable 'High Use' zones, and lists US Cabin Camp with 3 reservable sites. So the general 60/40 reservation statement is true for the park but not for the zones this itinerary camps in.

results.fact: Loss vs gain on a loop that returns to its trailhead
results.evidence: The trip is a loop from and back to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead, yet loss_ft is 9,300 against gain_ft 11,000 (itinerary days likewise sum to 9,300 loss / 11,000 gain). Only one source states a car-to-car figure for this loop (13,700 ft gained and lost); per the rules loss_ft is not set equal to gain_ft. Needs two sources for the loop's total descent.

The first-ascent writeup in the AAC journal gives the route as '2,000', IV 5.10b' with about 1,000 ft of loose upper-ridge scrambling; the route's page on a climbing database gives 2,000 ft (606 m), 12 pitches, and the FA party's own writeup also says about 2,000 ft. The individual pitch lengths (which sum to ~2,530 ft) are rope lengths including the long simul-climbed ridge and traverses, not the route's height, so length_m (the stated route length) should read ~610 m to agree with the October note; pitch lengths are left as published.

dist_km 27.4 km (17 mi) is the one-way approach shown as 'Approach (one way)'; the itinerary's ~36 mi is the out-and-back round trip ('close to 16 miles each way' plus the climb). Different quantities, consistent.
